disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.p1: This application is a purely informational and self-tracking tool based on current scientific literature (including Monash University guidelines and PubMed-indexed studies).
disclaimer.p2: The software does NOT provide medical diagnoses, does NOT prescribe therapies and does NOT replace in any way the opinion of a doctor, gastroenterologist or professional dietitian.
disclaimer.p3: Gastrointestinal disorders, including symptoms attributable to Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS), can overlap with more severe organic pathologies (such as celiac disease or chronic inflammatory bowel diseases - IBD).
disclaimer.p4: It is essential to perform clinical assessments and exclude other pathologies under the supervision of a specialist before undertaking a restrictive low-FODMAP diet. A prolonged and unguided exclusion diet can negatively alter the intestinal microbiota.
disclaimer.p5: Educational articles are summary publications: they cite sources but may not reflect the most recent evidence, so always verify the original studies. Do not modify prescribed therapies or diets for diagnosed pathologies (such as celiac disease, IBD or tumors) without consulting your doctor.
disclaimer.ai_text: This application uses AI-generated text. The information provided is general in nature and may not be up-to-date or complete. Always consult a healthcare professional for personalized medical advice.

app_subtitle: Scientific tool based on the FODMAP protocol and structural cellular requirements.
calc_activity_info: Sedentary: little or no exercise. Light: 1-3 days/week. Moderate: 3-5 days/week. Intense: 6-7 days/week
calc_allergies_message: If you have food allergies or intolerances, consult a doctor and adapt the suggested recipes and foods to your individual needs.
calc_medications_therapy_placeholder: Enter your medications here (e.g. Metformin 500mg, Levothyroxine 50mcg, Pantoprazole 20mg)...
calc_medication_recognized_text: Recognized: {{medication}} ({{brand}}). Configure therapy details to enable reminders and advanced calculations.
calc_diet_goal_info: Maintenance: maintain weight. Deficit: -500 kcal/day for weight loss. Surplus: +300 kcal/day for muscle gain
report_placeholder: Enter your biometric data and press "Calculate" to view personalized structural requirements.
report_energy_note: Total energy estimate: {{kcal}} kcal/day (Mifflin-St Jeor + activity level).
report_min_calorie_warning: Warning: calorie requirement has been limited to the physiological safety minimum (1200 kcal/day).
report_min_calorie_warning_male: Warning: calorie requirement has been limited to the physiological safety minimum (1500 kcal/day).
ibs_rec_d: With IBS-D, favor soluble fibers (psyllium, oats) and limit polyols and large lipid loads in a single meal: they reduce osmotic effect and modulate the gastrocolic reflex.
ibs_rec_c: With IBS-C, gradually increase fiber (mix soluble/insoluble) respecting water target: fiber without water further slows transit.
ibs_rec_m: With IBS-M, alternate attention to fermentables and soluble fiber: use the diary to understand which transit direction responds better to changes.
ibs_rec_unknown: Without a defined subtype, proceed by degrees: short low-FODMAP phase 1, then single reintroductions tracked in the diary.
filter_no_results: No food matches the search criteria or set filters.
diet_link_cta: Complete the calculator to connect your structural requirements to the diet phases.
diet_need_results: Complete the calculator to generate portioned meals based on your targets (grams, kcal, macros and micronutrients).
diet_reintroduced: Food in reintroduction (phase 3): include only if tolerated

medications.metformin_warning: Watch carbohydrates and fiber: metformin can increase gastrointestinal effects. Monitor blood sugar and transit.
medications.levothyroxine_warning: Watch calcium, coffee and soy: take it on an empty stomach and keep calcium/iron supplements at least 4 hours apart.
medications.antibiotics_warning: Antibiotics alter the microbiota: prefer probiotics away from dosing and fermented foods if tolerated.
medications.anticoagulants_warning: Keep vitamin K intake (leafy greens) stable and consult your doctor before changing your diet.
medications.diuretics_warning: Diuretics increase electrolyte loss: ensure adequate potassium and magnesium with your doctor.
medications.proton_pump_inhibitors_warning: Long-term use may reduce absorption of B12, magnesium and calcium: monitor levels.
medications.nsaids_warning: NSAIDs can irritate the gastric lining: take with food and limit alcohol.
medications.insulin_warning: Insulin requires constant glucose monitoring: coordinate meals and doses with your doctor. Watch for hypoglycemia with exercise or fasting.
medications.calcium_channel_blockers_warning: Calcium channel blockers may interact with grapefruit: avoid grapefruit juice. Monitor blood pressure and edema.
medications.statins_warning: Statins may cause muscle pain: report symptoms to your doctor. Avoid excess alcohol, monitor liver function.
medications.other_warning: Always consult your doctor or pharmacist before changing your diet when on medication.

bio_hacking_effect.protein: Protein slightly increased to support synthesis and satiety.
bio_hacking_effect.meal_window: Suggested eating window of about 10 hours (time-restricted eating).
bio_hacking_effect.micros: Optimize key micronutrients: magnesium, zinc, vitamin D, omega-3.

conditions.celiac_note: The targets shown are generic: follow the specialist's plan; the gluten-free diet is mandatory.
conditions.celiac_diet: Exclude all sources of gluten (wheat, barley, rye, contaminated oats); prefer rice, quinoa and certified gluten-free options.
conditions.diabetes_type1_note: For type 1 diabetes, monitor blood glucose and coordinate carbohydrates with insulin therapy.
conditions.diabetes_type1_effect: No calorie change; watch carbs and fiber ≥30 g/day
conditions.diabetes_type1_diet: Favor low-glycemic carbs and consistent portions; always align with your insulin plan and doctor.
conditions.diabetes_type2_note: For type 2 diabetes, favor low-glycemic carbs and regular physical activity.
conditions.diabetes_type2_effect: No calorie change; watch carbs and fiber ≥30 g/day
conditions.diabetes_type2_diet: Prefer low glycemic index carbohydrates (oats, quinoa, legumes if tolerated); avoid large carbohydrate loads in a single meal.
conditions.hypertension_note: Moderate added salt; use herbs and spices instead of sodium-rich condiments.
conditions.hypertension_diet: Limit added salt and aged cheeses; flavor with chives and garlic oil (low-FODMAP).
conditions.lactose_intolerance_note: Lactose-free milk or aged cheeses are already in line with the low-FODMAP approach.
conditions.lactose_intolerance_diet: Use lactose-free milk and aged cheeses (Parmigiano); avoid fresh cheeses with residual lactose. Generated meals automatically exclude milk and fresh cheeses.
conditions.pregnancy_note: In 2nd/3rd trimester needs increase: +300 kcal/day, protein and micronutrients (folate, iron, calcium, iodine).
conditions.pregnancy_diet: Increase protein intake (1.8 g/kg) and folate (600 µg), iron (27 mg), calcium (1300 mg) and iodine (220 µg). Ensure minimum calorie intake of 1200 kcal/day.
conditions.pregnancy_effect: +300 kcal/day; increases protein, folate, iron, calcium and iodine
conditions.menopause_note: Menopause slightly lowers basal metabolism and requires more attention to calcium and vitamin D for bone health.
conditions.menopause_diet: Favor calcium and vitamin D sources, fiber and protein to preserve lean mass; limit alcohol and ultra-processed foods.
conditions.menopause_effect: -5% calories; focus on calcium and vitamin D
conditions.pcos_note: PCOS does not directly change calories but requires attention to carbohydrates and insulin control.
conditions.pcos_diet: Prefer low glycemic index carbs, fiber ≥30 g/day and healthy fats; reduce simple sugars.
conditions.pcos_effect: No calorie change; focus on carbs and insulin
conditions.hypothyroidism_note: Hypothyroidism slows metabolism; limit raw goitrogenic foods and ensure adequate selenium and iodine.
conditions.hypothyroidism_diet: Cook cabbage, broccoli and cauliflower well; include Brazil nuts and fish for selenium/iodine. Consult your doctor for precise dosing.
conditions.celiac_effect: No calorie change; gluten-free diet mandatory
conditions.lactose_intolerance_effect: No calorie change; prefer lactose-free dairy
conditions.hyperthyroidism_note: Hyperthyroidism speeds up metabolism and increases calorie needs.
conditions.hyperthyroidism_diet: Slightly increase calories and protein; ensure calcium and vitamin D; avoid excess iodine without medical advice.
conditions.thyroid_note: Thyroid conditions (hypothyroidism/hyperthyroidism) alter metabolism and iodine, selenium, zinc needs. Watch for goitrogenic foods in hypothyroidism.
conditions.thyroid_diet: For hypothyroidism, avoid raw goitrogenic foods in large amounts (cabbage, broccoli, cauliflower, soy). Ensure adequate selenium (Brazil nuts) and iodine intake. Always consult your doctor for potential supplementation.

warnings.protein_deficiency: Protein deficiency: increase protein intake to support tissues and the immune system.
warnings.fiber_deficiency: Fiber deficiency: increase vegetable, fruit and whole grain intake for the microbiota.
warnings.iron_deficiency: Iron deficiency: increase meat, legume, spinach or fortified food intake.
warnings.vitamin_d_deficiency: Vitamin D deficiency: consider supplementation or increase sun exposure (consult doctor).
warnings.calcium_deficiency: Calcium deficiency: increase dairy, leafy green or fortified food intake.

workout_show_exercise: Show exercise and how to perform it
workout_squat_desc: The squat strengthens legs and core. Keep feet shoulder-width apart, maintain a neutral spine, and descend as if sitting in a chair.
workout_squat_steps: Lower by bending knees and hips, back straight
Push up through the heels and squeeze glutes at the top
workout_pushup_desc: A strength exercise for chest, shoulders and triceps. Can be performed on the floor or with knees down to reduce load.
workout_pushup_steps: Start in a plank, hands under shoulders
Lower chest until nearly touching the floor
Push back up, keeping core engaged
workout_plank_desc: Isometric hold for core and lower-back stability. Useful for posture and avoiding abdominal overload.
workout_plank_steps: Keep body aligned from head to heels
Breathe and hold without sagging hips
workout_lunge_desc: Lunges improve balance and lower-body strength with controlled load on the abdomen.
workout_lunge_steps: Lower hips until both knees are at 90°
Push back up and alternate legs
workout_burpees_desc: High-intensity full-body cardiovascular exercise. Modify by removing the jump if needed.
workout_burpees_steps: From standing, drop into a squat
Jump feet back into a plank
Optional push-up, return to squat and jump
workout_biceps_curl_desc: Dumbbell exercise to strengthen biceps. Keep elbows fixed at your sides.
workout_shoulder_press_desc: Press weights overhead with dumbbells or a barbell to develop shoulders and triceps.
workout_shoulder_press_steps: Dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward
Press weights up until arms are extended
Lower with control without arching back
workout_row_desc: Pulling exercise for lats and rhomboids, performed with dumbbell, barbell or cable.
workout_row_steps: Hinge forward with a flat back
Pull weight toward hip, squeezing back
workout_calf_raise_desc: Raise heels to strengthen calves. Simple, bodyweight or loaded.
workout_calf_raise_steps: Stand with toes on a step or floor
Lift heels as high as possible
workout_incompatible_filter: Exercise not compatible with active filter
workout_suggestion_no_data: Fill in the calculator to receive a personalized plan.
workout_suggestion_deficit: Caloric deficit goal: prefer walking, swimming and bodyweight metabolic circuits.
workout_suggestion_surplus: Caloric surplus goal: focus on squats, push-ups and rows to stimulate lean mass.
workout_suggestion_sedentary: Sedentary lifestyle: start with walking and gentle mobility to get your body used to movement.
workout_suggestion_active: High activity level: add dumbbell strength work to support metabolism and joints.
workout_suggestion_balanced: Balanced plan: alternate cardio, bodyweight strength and active recovery.

fodmap_lactose_banner_text: The Low-FODMAP diet is naturally low in lactose. During the elimination phase, all lactose-containing dairy products (milk, yogurt, fresh cheese, cream) are excluded. Allowed: lactose-free dairy products, aged cheeses (Parmesan, Grana Padano, Pecorino ≥24 months), butter and ghee. Lactose-free products contain added lactase enzyme that breaks down milk sugar into glucose and galactose – they are safe. During the reintroduction phase (Phase 3), test your personal lactose tolerance gradually. Always consult a doctor or dietitian if you have diagnosed lactose intolerance.

info.calc_weight: Body weight is the main input used to estimate basal metabolic rate with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation.
info.calc_height: Height, together with weight, determines body surface area and baseline energy needs.
info.calc_age: Age affects basal metabolic rate, which tends to decrease over the years.
info.calc_sex: Biological sex changes average lean mass and therefore resting energy expenditure.
info.calc_activity: Activity level multiplies basal metabolic rate to obtain total daily energy expenditure. Sedentary (1.2): little or no exercise, desk job. Light activity (1.375): light exercise or walking 1-3 days per week. Moderate activity (1.55): moderate exercise or sports 3-5 days per week. Intense activity (1.725): intense workouts or heavy physical work 6-7 days per week. Very intense activity (1.9): heavy twice-daily training or professional athletes.
info.calc_ibs: Select your IBS subtype to get tailored advice on fiber and FODMAP intake.
info.condition_diabetes_type1: Type 1 diabetes is insulin-dependent: carbohydrates must be balanced with insulin therapy and frequent glucose monitoring.
info.condition_diabetes_type2: Type 2 diabetes is often associated with insulin resistance: nutrition favors complex carbohydrates, fiber and weight control.
info.condition_hypertension: With hypertension the calculator suggests moderating sodium without changing calories.
info.condition_hypothyroidism: Hypothyroidism slows metabolism: calories are reduced by about 7%.
info.condition_hyperthyroidism: Hyperthyroidism speeds up metabolism: calories are increased by about 7%.
info.condition_celiac: Celiac disease requires a gluten-free diet; generic targets must be confirmed by a specialist.
info.condition_pregnancy: During pregnancy the calculator adds 300 kcal/day and increases protein, folate, iron and calcium.
info.condition_menopause: In menopause metabolism slightly decreases; the focus shifts to calcium and vitamin D.
info.condition_pcos: PCOS calls attention to low-glycemic carbohydrates and fiber ≥30 g/day.
info.allergen_gluten: Wheat, barley, rye and contaminated oats. Must be avoided in celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
info.allergen_crustaceans: Shrimp, crab, lobster and similar. A common and often severe allergen.
info.allergen_eggs: Hen and other bird eggs. Watch out for albumen and bakery products.
info.allergen_fish: Fresh, preserved fish or extracts. Can be present in sauces and condiments.
info.allergen_peanuts: Peanuts and derivatives. Reactions can be severe; always read labels.
info.allergen_soy: Soy, tofu, soy sauce and lecithin. Common in processed foods.
info.allergen_milk: Milk and fresh dairy. In this app you can filter and prefer lactose-free alternatives.
info.allergen_milk_fodmap: The FODMAP diet is lactose-free: only lactose-free or aged dairy (e.g. Parmesan) is allowed.
info.allergen_tree_nuts: Almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts, pistachios, cashews and similar.
info.allergen_celery: Celery, celeriac and seeds. Often used as a flavoring.
info.allergen_mustard: Mustard seeds, flour or sauce. Used as a condiment in many dishes.
info.allergen_sesame: Sesame seeds and oil. Present in hummus, tahini and baked goods.
info.allergen_lupins: Lupin beans and lupin flour. May appear in gluten-free baked products.
info.allergen_sulphites: Sulphites used as preservatives in wine, dried fruit and packaged foods.
info.diet_goal: Maintenance keeps weight stable; deficit reduces by 500 kcal; surplus adds 300 kcal to support lean mass.
info.medications: Enter your medications to receive warnings about interactions with foods, fiber or micronutrients.
info.bio_hacking: Enables evidence-based tweaks: slightly higher protein, ~10-hour eating window, focus on key micronutrients.
info.filter_category: Groups foods by macrocategory (carbohydrates, proteins, vegetables, fruit, condiments).
info.filter_month: Show only foods in season for the selected month: often fresher, cheaper and more nutritious.
info.fodmap_Fruttani: Fructans: chains of fructose found in wheat, garlic, onion and some vegetables. Highly fermentable.
info.fodmap_Lattosio: Lactose: milk sugar. Can cause symptoms in people with intolerance or malabsorption.
info.fodmap_Fruttosio: Fructose: sugar from fruit and honey. Excess over glucose can ferment in the gut.
info.fodmap_Galattani: Galactans: oligosaccharides in legumes. Often responsible for bloating after beans and lentils.
info.fodmap_Polioli: Polyols: sweeteners such as sorbitol and xylitol and some fruits (e.g. plums, peaches). Can have osmotic effects.
info.fodmap_high: High FODMAP content: limit during the elimination phase and reintroduce cautiously.
info.fodmap_low: Low FODMAP content: generally well tolerated during elimination, in appropriate portions.
info.workout_equipment_filter: Choose whether to show only bodyweight exercises or gym-based exercises.
info.workout_generate_suggested: Automatically creates a week of workouts based on your calorie goal and activity level.
info.workout_exercise_selector: Change the exercise for each day: duration adjusts based on the selection.
info.recipe_servings: Indicates how many people the recipe is for. Ingredients remain in total grams.
info.recipe_ingredients: Each ingredient is given in grams. You can freely adjust amounts based on tolerance.
info.shopping_category: Categories help organize shopping by supermarket department.
info.shopping_quantity: Enter the required weight or volume. You can use g, kg, ml or pieces.
info.diet_phase: The diet is split into phases: adaptation, FODMAP elimination, reintroduction and personalization.
info.diet_reintroduced: In phase 3 single FODMAP groups are reintroduced to test individual tolerance.
info.diary_symptoms: Select the symptoms you felt and rate severity: this helps correlate foods and wellbeing.
info.diary_transit: 1-3 = slowed transit, 4 = optimal, 5-7 = accelerated. Pick the value that best describes your day.
